Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The players are out in the middle. Matt Henry to bowl first. John Campbell and Tagenarine Chanderpaul to open for West Indies.
...THE CHASE....

The hosts aimed to get the lead over 500 and got it done easily, having already secured 481 runs before the start of today's play. West Indies kept it simple and made New Zealand make mistakes. Kemar Roach ended with a five-fer while Ojay Shields and Jayden Seales picked the remaining three wickets. Now, it's a huge target in front of the visitors. Rather than looking at it, they'll try to bat through this session before losing any wickets. Can the openers start well? Let's find out.

So, as expected New Zealand have declared with Nathan Smith only the batter left while Tom Blundell ruled out of the game. They have set a mammoth target of 531 runs for West Indies to chase. New Zealand batted for 14 overs and as thought, it wasn't just defending at all. They chased everything and in the process added 49 runs while losing 4 wickets.

The big question this morning is how long the Kiwis will bat before declaring. With Michael Bracewell and Will Young at the crease, we might see some quick runs before they invite the West Indies to begin a mammoth chase. Stay tuned as we get underway for what promises to be a decisive day.

For the West Indies, it has been a grueling experience in the field. Despite Kemar Roach and Ojay Shields picking up two wickets each, the missed opportunities early in Ravindra's innings proved too costly. New Zealand now sits comfortably with a lead of 481 runs, leaving the visitors with a mountain to climb.

Welcome back to the Hagley Oval for Day 4. If yesterday was anything to go by, New Zealand is firmly in the driver's seat after a dominant display with the bat. Day 3 belonged entirely to the hosts, featuring spectacular centuries from Tom Latham and Rachin Ravindra that left the West Indies bowlers searching for answers. The highlight was the massive 279-run partnership between the two left-handers. While Latham played a precise and classy knock of 145, Ravindra made the visitors pay for early dropped catches to smash a brilliant 176. Their combined effort has effectively batted the opposition out of the game.

After the first session, West Indies have been chasing the game and with the lead nearing the 500-mark, the visitors have been pushed out of the game already. New Zealand are hungry for more and will try and add some quick runs on Day 4 before making West Indies dance to their tunes. Join us for the action of Day 4 at 10 pm GMT (previous day). Join us an hour earlier for the build-up. Till then, cheers!

The third session started in a similar pattern, with the Kiwis milking runs effectively. Rachin Ravindra and Tom Latham batted beautifully, both on course to double up their respective centuries, but Latham fell on 145 to Kemar Roach. Rachin Ravindra continued his merry way but he too fell on 176 to a wonderful yorker by Ojay Shields in the final hour of the session.

However, the afternoon session completely flipped the script as the West Indies paid a heavy price for sloppy fielding and dropped catches. The momentum swung firmly back to New Zealand as Captain Tom Latham and Rachin Ravindra stitched together a flawless partnership. Latham notched up a brilliant 14th Test century, leaving the West Indies searching for answers as the game began to slip away.

The morning session was a true rollercoaster of fortunes. New Zealand looked to build a commanding lead, but the West Indies kept fighting to stay in the contest. Just as the hosts seemed comfortable, the Windies struck crucial blows, removing Devon Conway and then delivering a massive shock by dismissing Kane Williamson, right on the stroke of lunch. With Tom Blundell already ruled out due to injury, the Kiwis were effectively three wickets down.

New Zealand have rolled over West Indies. Day 3 has moved at a rapid pace, with New Zealand extending their lead to 481 runs and are hungry for more. It was all possible because of the marathon partnership between Tom Latham and Rachin Ravindra. After losing Devon Conway in the first session and also Kane Williamson at the stroke of Lunch, West Indies had their tails up but Latham and Ravindra showed incredible character to fight it through.

After a shaky start, Shai Hope and Tagenarine Chanderpaul steadied the ship with gritty half-centuries, but things unraveled quickly after tea. A hostile spell from Jacob Duffy, who claimed his maiden five-wicket haul, saw the visitors slip from a comfortable 100/2 to being bowled out, handing New Zealand a vital 64-run lead on the first innings.

Hello everyone and welcome back to our coverage of Day 3. The match has moved forward at a rapid pace, and as we head into this morning's session, the home side sits firmly in the driver's seat. With a lead of 96 runs and all ten wickets still intact, the Kiwis will be looking to bat the visitors completely out of the contest today.

Day 3 is going to be the 'Moving Day' and the stakes will be high! Will the Kiwis continue their dominance or will the Windies stage a comeback? The game took a dramatic turn as Duffy's brilliant bowling in the final session swung the game in the Kiwis' favor, with the Windies being bowled out for 167. Duffy's 5-wicket haul, Henry's 3 wickets, and Zak's 2 wickets sealed the lead of 64 for the Kiwis. Despite Hope and Chanderpaul's half-centuries, the Windies' batting lineup failed to fire, leaving them behind in the game. The Kiwis, on the other hand, ended the day on a high, scoring 32 without loss in their second innings.

In the afternoon session, after a promising start, where Shai Hope reached his fifty alongside a solid Tagenarine Chanderpaul, West Indies suffered a dramatic mid-session collapse triggered by New Zealand's bowlers. Jacob Duffy broke the stand using the short ball to dismiss Hope, while Matt Henry followed up with a lethal double-strike in a single over, removing Roston Chase and Justin Greaves for ducks to slide the visitors from 100/2 to 106/5. Tevin Imlach joined Chanderpaul to stem the rot with defensive resilience to steer the side to 120/5 at the tea break.

With Roston Chase refusing to bowl a part-time spinner, the umpires have called it STUMPS ON DAY 2! In the opening session, West Indies displayed resilience to reach lunch on Day 2 at 68/2, trailing New Zealand by 163 runs, after a turbulent start to their first innings. Following New Zealand's rapid dismissal for 231 by Jayden Seales, the Caribbean side was initially rocked by Zakary Foulkes and Matt Henry, crumbling to 10/2 with the cheap losses of John Campbell and Alick Athanaze. However, Shai Hope and Tagenarine Chanderpaul arrested the slide with a gritty, unbeaten 58-run partnership, successfully defying the Kiwi pace attack to stabilize the innings before the lunch break.
